idiom_name: empty interface plus generic bounds and reified is-checks
implementation_notes: Kotlin interfaces may be empty and Kotlin inherits the JVM's marker-interface ecosystem (java.io.Serializable, Cloneable), so the classic form works directly: declare an empty interface, implement it, and constrain generics or use is checks. Kotlin adds reified type parameters so generic runs of is/filterIsInstance work without erasure surprises. Use it when conformance must be nominal and visible to Java code too; annotations fit metadata better.
code_sketch:
interface Deletable

class Order : Deletable

inline fun <reified T : Deletable> List<Any>.deletables(): List<T> = filterIsInstance<T>()
pitfalls: is-checks on generic types need reified type parameters; erased types fail silently in non-inline code.
Kotlin interfaces cannot hold state, which suits markers but blocks evolving a marker into a hybrid contract later.
An empty interface is indistinguishable from a forgotten supertype without documentation.

variants.name: Sealed interface as a closed marked set
variants.implementation_notes: A sealed interface restricts implementations to the same module and package and makes when exhaustive, so a closed set of marked types is expressed and checked at compile time with no separate marker test; implementations may be data classes or enums and can implement several sealed interfaces at once. Use it where the set is closed and consumers switch over it; keep a plain marker interface where third parties must be able to opt in.
variants.code_sketch:
sealed interface Primitive

data class Text(val v: String) : Primitive
data class Num(val n: Int) : Primitive

fun render(p: Primitive) = when (p) {
    is Text -> p.v
    is Num -> p.n.toString()
}
pitfalls: Sealed interfaces cannot be implemented in other modules (Kotlin 1.5+ rules), so they cannot model open categories.
when-exhaustiveness holds only on the sealed subject's static type; an Any subject silently needs an else branch.
Every exhaustive when must be revisited when the set changes - compile-time churn in exchange for compile-time safety.

variants.name: Annotation class as a metadata marker
variants.implementation_notes: Annotation classes carry metadata without creating a type - the analogue of a Java marker annotation, and the mechanism kotlin.DslMarker itself uses (a meta-annotation with no fields, applied to other annotations). Read them with reflection through KClass.annotations, or consume them with an annotation processor. They cannot appear in generic constraints, so they do not replace the interface when compile-time substitutability is required.
pitfalls: Reflection-based annotation checks are a runtime decision and cost more than a type check.
Kotlin's default retention is RUNTIME; choosing SOURCE keeps the check out of the binary but also out of reflection.
Annotation classes cannot implement interfaces, be extended, or be used as generic constraints.
